title: stroke_sculpt must not turn the mesh inside out
user-messages: also the sculpting tools allow for the mesh to go inside out
for mesh-78 how much time does the new unflod add, and that method seems to be quite long is there any reuse we are missing?
description:
stroke_sculpt lets the mesh go inside out: a displacement can carry vertices past their neighbours, flipping faces so the back side shows. The blind skull run MESH-75 (archived as archive/mesh-75; its layers are dsl/skull/ in that tag) shows it from below: a triangular fold in the middle of the skull base and a flap at each jaw angle, drawn in the viewer's back-face colour. They came from the strongest strokes: skull_base at strength 2.0 and the jaw layer's Front stroke drawn 2.5x past its trace.

Displacement must never invert a face. Find where the inversion happens (opposing displacements of neighbouring strokes, silhouette drags pulling a region through itself, strength above 1 overshooting, symmetrising averaging a vertex with a far twin) and prevent it in StrokeSculpt, for example by limiting each vertex's step so no incident face flips, or by relaxing the region after displacement; choose and justify.

Reuse note: PATCH-127 (patch-127 worktree, REVIEW) adds MeshFoldRelaxation in geometry/mesh/data/ops/ (detects faces folded against the summed normals of their corners and relaxes their neighbourhood, or refuses), and MESH-77 adds a general smooth_mesh operation. Build on those rather than a third fold detector or smoother.

Rework (user, 2026-11-01): MeshSmoothing.unfold costs about 6 s on the skull (4.1 s to 10.1 s), and much of its ~140 lines re-implements code the repo already has. Before landing, rebase it onto MESH-86's one-pass sculpt and fold in this reuse and speed work:
1. One fold test. master now has the same rule in QuadLayoutNode.requireParameters (PATCH-127: a face's unit normal against the summed unit normals at its corners); MeshSmoothing.foldedFaces is that rule plus an angle threshold and is a single-caller helper. Make one shared method (geometry/mesh/data/ops) used by quad_layout's refusal and by unfold.
2. One ray query that skips the faces at its own ends. unfold walks past triangles touching the ray's own vertices twice (edge crossings, and each vertex's clearance). Add it to TriangleBvh (nearest hit ignoring triangles that touch given vertices) and use it in both places, and wherever the one-pass sculpt's visibility rays need the same.
3. Refit, don't rebuild. Each shortening round calls surface.build() from scratch although only positions change; add an in-place refit of the boxes to TriangleBvh, and re-test only edges near vertices whose step changed, not every edge each round.
4. Share the BVH: DisplacementSum (MESH-86) already builds one over the base; unfold, wired into the one-pass code, uses it rather than its own.
5. The ring-taper loop at the end of unfold repeats umbrella's neighbour-average loop in the same file; share it.
definition-of-done:
1. MESH-75's skull layers (git show archive/mesh-75) evaluate with no inverted face: a count of faces whose normal flips against their pre-displacement normal is zero, and a bottom-view capture under tmp/ shows no back faces.
2. A StrokeSculptTest case that inverts faces on the current code (e.g. two opposing strong strokes, or a silhouette drag through the surface) passes with the fix.
3. Existing sculpts (dsl/stroke_sculpt_head.dsl and the skull layers) look the same elsewhere: before/after captures under tmp/.
4. The cause of each inversion found is named in changes-made.

5. The rework above: one shared fold test used by quad_layout and unfold; the skip-own-ends ray query and an in-place refit on TriangleBvh; unfold in the one-pass sculpt using DisplacementSum's BVH; the skull's load time with and without unfold measured on the run-4 sculpt (skull4) and reported, the unfold share well under the 6 s it costs now.
testing-plan: 1. Run StrokeSculptTest. 2. Evaluate the archive/mesh-75 skull layers and count inverted faces before and after. 3. Capture the skull and head demo from below and from the front before and after.
changes-made: Causes found (archive/mesh-75 skull layers, counted per pass): (1) silhouette drags pleat the surface over itself — shape and skull_base turned 40 and 80 faces over, the jaw-angle flaps and the skull-base fold; the pleat is smooth, so the MESH-77 own-corner fold test misses it. (2) fills pushed through other surface: eye_sockets' mirrored pits (each a straight push along its seeds' mean normal, which points sideways) meet through the nose bridge, nasal_opening punches through, 1314 and 4130 inward faces; no face flips, the surface crosses itself. (3) refinement's Phong lift folds faces across sharp rims of earlier passes (15 at cheekbones). Strength above 1 and relaxing only amplify these; symmetrising added nothing measurable.

Fix, at the source: MeshSmoothing.unfold (shared with MESH-77's umbrella, which now calls it) shortens a move per vertex until no face folds against its own corners (MESH-77 definition), none turns more than 120 degrees against the corner normals it started with (a pleat's middle; steep pit walls past 90 degrees stay legal), and, when asked, no edge passes through a face (TriangleBvh). Steps start at half their clearance from the unmoved surface; failures halve the steps of the involved corners, tapered over the ring, then cancel. StrokeSculpt calls it on each pass's final step (after relax and symmetrise) with crossings on, and on refinement's Phong lift against the flat split. Chosen over relaxing afterwards: relaxation moves vertices the sculptor did not ask to move and still needs a fold test to stop; limiting the step leaves everything that was valid exactly as drawn (head demo captures pixel-identical).

Tests: StrokeSculptTest.aPitDeeperThanTheBodyStopsShortOfTheFarSide (1008 inward faces without the fix, 0 with) and twoPitsSunkTowardEachOtherDoNotPassThrough (830 without, 0 with; the thin-wall/mirrored-pit case MESH-79's jaw floor hit). Skull inward faces per layer before/after in tmp/mesh-78-measurements.json: final 13834 to 0; nasal_opening..teeth keep 2 (gone after subdivision). Captures tmp/mesh-78-{skull,head}-{before,after}-{front,below,multiview}.png. Known cost: zigzag rims where the eye sockets meet the nose bridge, where steps were cut back piecewise; skull load 4.1 s to 10.1 s for the per-round crossing test.

Rework (2026-11-01), stacked on MESH-86's one-pass sculpt: the limiter runs once on the pass's summed step (after relax and symmetrise) in StrokeSculpt, and MidpointSplit pulls its Phong lift back toward the flat split (cause 3). Reuse: (1) MeshFolds (geometry/mesh/data/ops) is the one fold test; QuadLayoutNode.requireParameters reads new MeshFolds(...).foldedAtStart and unfold calls update() each round, which re-tests only faces whose normal or a corner's normal changed; MeshSmoothing.foldedFaces is gone. (2) TriangleBvh.nearestHitAvoiding skips triangles with a marked corner, used by both of unfold's former walk-past loops (edge crossings, step clearance); DisplacementSum's visibility rays use a slack bound, not a walk-past, so they are unchanged. (3) TriangleBvh.refit refits boxes in place; unfold re-tests only edges of faces around vertices whose step changed, then every edge once before accepting. (4) unfold takes DisplacementSum's BVH (built over the unmoved refined surface) instead of building its own, and leaves it fitted to the result. (5) umbrella and the ring taper share neighbourMean. Speed: a bounded ray now rejects leaf triangles by their box first; the taper spreads only the round's own cut (it used to re-lower a ring further out every round, 30 rounds of growing re-tests).

Measured on the run-4 skull (mesh-88 round05, copied to tmp/skull4; 136521 vertices after refinement), warm loads: without unfold 1.5 s, inward faces 15; with unfold 3.8 s (was 7.0 s after the rebase with the old structure), inward faces 4 (the base.ply's own 4). Unfold's share is about 2.3 s, down from about 5.5 s. Eye sockets deeper than the run-4 limit of 0.22 (tmp/skull4-eyes0.35, -eyes0.5): without unfold 12536 and 35233 inward faces, sockets punching through; with unfold 4 and 4. At 0.35 the floor sinks about 0.11 further and stays clean except a crumpled rim where the socket meets the nasal cavity; at 0.5 the whole floor crumples (steps cut back piecewise), so the limiter prevents inversion but does not make a clean socket past about 0.35. Head demo pixel-identical with and without. StrokeSculptTest pit tests: 1008 and 830 inward faces without, 0 with. MESH-75's layered skull no longer evaluates (one-pass refuses a stroke_sculpt of a stroke_sculpt), so the skull checks use run 4. Captures tmp/mesh-78-skull4-{before,after}-*, tmp/mesh-78-skull4-eyes{0.35,0.5}-*, tmp/mesh-78-head-{before,after}-*; profiles tmp/profile-with-unfold*.html.
review-summary: stroke_sculpt, now on MESH-86's one-pass sculpt, shortens a pass's summed step wherever it would fold a face or push the surface through another. Without it deep pits and silhouette drags turn the skull inside out; the limiter shares quad_layout's fold test and the sculpt's BVH.
